item.research_question: How can severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing be used to tailor heterogeneous microstructures and overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in brittle intermetallic-containing high entropy alloys?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2 high entropy alloy (FCC matrix with complex Laves phase particles)
item.processing_route: Homogenized ingots (1200 °C/24 h) were multi-pass cold- or cryo-rolled to 90% reduction in thickness (final thickness ~0.4 mm); cryo-rolling involved immersion in liquid N2 for 0.5 h before and after every pass; subsequent annealing at 800 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching.
item.test_conditions: Tensile tests conducted at ambient temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1 using dog-bone shaped specimens.
key_findings: Cryo-rolling resulted in a finer lamellar nanostructure with an average HAB spacing of ~50 ± 9 nm compared to ~65 ± 12 nm in cold-rolled samples.
The Laves phase particles showed greater fragmentation in cryo-rolled samples (average size ~0.68 ± 0.40 µm) compared to cold-rolled samples (~1.00 ± 0.44 µm).
The cryo-rolled and annealed HEA achieved a yield strength of 1219 ± 14 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 1272 ± 25 MPa with ~22% elongation.
The cold-rolled and annealed HEA showed a yield strength of 774 ± 13 MPa and ultimate tensile strength of 1085 ± 18 MPa with ~20% elongation.
The yield strength of the cryo-rolled and annealed HEA was increased by ~400 MPa (~58% increase) compared to the cold-rolled and annealed HEA.
The cryo-rolled and annealed HEA exhibited a heterogeneous microstructure with co-existing deformed and recrystallized regions, whereas the cold-rolled HEA was predominantly recrystallized.

Profuse ε nano-precipitates formed early in the cryo-rolled HEA (after 120 s at 800 °C), inhibiting recrystallization via Zener pinning, while precipitation lagged recrystallization in the cold-rolled HEA.
item.mechanism: The heterogeneous microstructure originates from accelerated precipitation of the nanosized ε phase early in the recrystallization process due to a greater density of nucleation sites (dislocations, shear bands, grain boundaries) in the cryo-rolled HEA; these precipitates pin high-angle boundaries (Zener pinning), inhibiting recrystallization and creating a mix of deformed and recrystallized regions; mechanical incompatibility between these domains generates strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs), creating long-range back stress that delays necking and enhances both strength and ductility.
item.limitations: The back stress generated by the heterogeneous microstructure was not quantified in this study.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the results indicate significant opportunities for achieving novel heterogeneous microstructures in a wide range of HEAs through innovative processing by cryo-rolling.
quotes: Cryo-rolling resulted in a finer lamellar nanostructure and decidedly greater fragmentation of the Laves phase.
The novel heterogeneous microstructure of the cryo-rolled and annealed HEA resulted in a remarkable enhancement in strength-ductility synergy.
The formation of the nano-precipitates can effectively pin the migration of the HABs, thereby significantly inhibiting the progress of recrystallization due to the Zener pinning effect.
